topic: Nanbeige4.3-33B vs Qwen 3.8: the self-reported coding claim and what fits one card
title: The 33B coder test: claim vs card
hook_text: Nanbeige or Qwen, one number decides.
hook_candidates: Nanbeige or Qwen, one number decides.
Eighty point nine. The challenger graded itself.
The new 33B claims Qwen's coding crown.
You run Qwen. A 33B wants your card.
One table, two winners, your twenty-four gigabytes.
Sixty point three versus sixty-one point seven. Qwen wins.
Ten days old, ninety-nine quants, one loud claim.
Which 33B coder earns your download tonight?
The 33B that says it beats Qwen at code.
narration_full: Nanbeige or Qwen, one number decides. You already run Qwen on your twenty-four gigabyte card. Its own card claims eighty point nine on Terminal-Bench, which scores real terminal tasks. Qwen, same table: seventy-three. Every number, self-reported. Same table, next row. SWE-Bench Pro, software engineering benchmarks, scores fixing real GitHub issues. Nanbeige posts sixty point three. Qwen posts sixty-one point seven. It bolded that one too. Now what fits. Nanbeige's quant, a compressed copy of the weights, is twenty point seven nine gigabytes on disk. Qwen's four-bit build runs smaller. The rule: one real coding task, both quants, same settings. Keep whichever your terminal crowns.
